plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of bright yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. The heads track the sun when young, and the plant is grown worldwide for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, Argentina, and China
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soil and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere, with peak harvest in July and early August
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the US
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with drooping pinkish-purple petals around a prominent spiky, orange-brown central cone. It is popular in pollinator gardens and tolerates heat and drought well.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern North America; widely grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiky central cone, and goldfinches love to eat its seeds in late summer.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a self-cleaning, water-repellent surface.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September) in the Northern Hemisphere, peaking in July and August
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; cultivated in ponds across India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; seeds around 1,300 years old have been successfully germinated, and the flower is sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism.
